sentences.text:
Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal, challenging the order dated 28.02.2019 ("the impugned order" in short) of Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (Central),
14, Darya Ganj, New Delhi ("ADM" in short), whereby he imposed penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ (Rupees one lac and fifty thousand only) upon the appellant under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short), for selling substandard milk in contravention to Section 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) & 27(1) of FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zx) of FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation 1.2.11 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard & Food Additives), Regulations, 2011 {FSS(FPS & FA)} Regulations in short).
2.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard & Food Additives), Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that on 16.04.2018, a sample of "Mixed Milk" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the premises of appellant i.e. M/s Om Diary,
Shop No. 6132, BlockI, Dev Nagar, Karol Bagh, New Delhi110005.

On analysis by the Food Analyst, Delhi, the said sample was declared to be substandard vide report dt.24.04.2018 due to the presence of milk powder which should not be present as per the definition of mixed milk laid down under Regulation 1.2.11 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products FSAT No. 10/19 Sh.
Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 2 of 7 Standards & Food Additives) Regulation, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety & Standards (Food Products FSAT No. 10/19
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: After receipt the said report of Food Analyst, Delhi, the appellant herein was provided with an opportunity to file an appeal under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act within the stipulated period of 30 days.
Consequently, a complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before the Adjudicating Officer.
After pleadings and enquiry, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 28.02.2019 imposing a penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ upon the appellant.
3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter alia on the grounds among others that the Ld. ADM has failed to appreciate that the Food Analyst has not given the percentage of milk powder.
The sample was also fit for human consumption.
The test skimmed milk powder was found to be positive.
Ld. Adjudication Officer did not conduct fair enquiry in a legal way or that no departmental witness or other witnesses were examined.
4. The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal.

5. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State and have perused the records and also gone through the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Chief PP for the State.
6. The Ld.
Counsel for the appellant argued that the Food Analyst has not given percentage of milk powder in the sample taken from the FBO.
Even, the sampled commodity was fit for human consumption FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 3 of 7 and the same was not injurious to health.

sentences.text: The Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor argued that as the powder is prohibited in the milk, there is no question of showing percentage of powder in the report.
The milk powder was found in the sample and it was not natural milk and the same has also been considered by the Ld. ADM in the impugned order dt.28.02.2019.
In the natural milk, no powder can be mixed.

The standards and parameters,
which have been laid down by the legislature are to be followed but the appellant has not followed it for selling the milk in this case.
The substandard milk is to be treated as an adulterated article, even if it has not caused injuries to health.

The appellant did not comply with the standards of rules /
regulations of Food Safety and Standard Act.
Therefore, the impugned order has been rightly FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr.

. The Ld. Chief PP for the State, in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar versus The State of Uttar Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No. 1541 of 2019 decided on 04.10.2019 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India 8.

sentences.text:
In the present case, the appellant has challenged the impugned order dt.28.02.2019 mainly on the grounds that the sampled commodity was fit for human consumption and that the percentage of milk powder was not given in the Food Analyst Report dated 24.04.2018.
9.

The Food Analyst vide his report dated 24.04.2018, opined the sample as substandard due to the presence of milk powder which should not be present as per the definition of mixed milk laid down under Regulation 1.2.11 of the FS&S (FPS & FA) Regulation, 2011.

The appellant herein was duly provided with an opportunity by the Ld. ADM to file an appeal under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act within the stipulated period of 30 days against the report of Food Analyst.
However, no appeal was preferred by the appellant.
10. It is also an admitted fact that milk powder was present in the sampled commodity and it was not natural milk.
As per the definition and standards of Mixed Milk, the presence of milk powder should be absent.
11. Section 26 of the FSS Act 2006 provides responsibilities of the Food Business Operator.

Sub clause (2)(ii) of Section 26 the said Act provides that no Food Business Operator shall himself or by any person on FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 5 of 7 his behalf manufacturer, store, sell or distribute any article of food which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter.

entities.text: FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 26 of the FSS Act, 2006, seeks to provide for the responsibilities of the food business operator to ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import,
distribution and sale within the businesses under his control.

Subclause (2) provides that no food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacturer, store, sell or distribute any article of food which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter or which is for the time being prohibited by the Food Authority or the Central Government or the State Government in the interest of public health.

sentences.text: In view of the above facts and circumstances, arguments on behalf of the parties and the materials available on reocrd and also the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant and the Ld. Chief PP for the State, I am of the considered opinion that the sample food article i.e. "Mixed Milk" did not conform to the specified standard as laid down in Regulation 1.2.11 FSS (FPS & FA) Regulations.

Nonconforming to the specified standard rendered the sample i.e.
Mixed Milk as substandard in terms of Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act.
The parameters and standards laid down by the legislatures were not followed by the appellant for selling the milk.
The substandard milk is to be treated as an adulterated article, even if it has not caused injuries to health.

The judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant are FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 6 of 7 distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case.

entities.text: FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the appellant has failed to demonstrate any justified reason to interfere with the impugned order dt.28.02.2019 of the Ld. ADM.
Section 51 of FSS Act prescribes a maximum penalty of Rs.5,00,000/ (Rupees Five Lacs only).
However, the Ld. ADM imposed a penalty of Rs.1,50,000 lacs upon the appellant.

Therefore, this court also deem it fit that the said penalty of Rs.1,50,000/
is a meager amount, if the maximum amount of penalty of Rs.5,00,000/ is considered for selling substandard milk.
Accordingly, this appeal is devoid of any merits and the same is dismissed.
Copy of this Judgment along with the record of the Ld. ADM be sent to the Ld. ADM.
Appeal file be consigned to record room.
